claims.text: CodePipeline's default execution mode is `SUPERSEDED`.
In CodePipeline's `SUPERSEDED` execution mode, a stage is locked to one execution at a time.
In CodePipeline `SUPERSEDED` mode, a newer execution can overtake and drop an earlier execution that is still waiting to enter a locked stage, before it ever starts.

In CodePipeline `SUPERSEDED` mode, if a CodeBuild stage running `pulumi up` is busy and enough commits land, a queued execution waiting behind it can be superseded and never run, silently skipping a deployment.
Setting a CodePipeline pipeline's execution mode to `QUEUED` makes waiting executions form a queue and each runs in turn.
CodePipeline's `QUEUED` execution mode requires a V2 pipeline type.
The AWS CLI's `create-pipeline` and `update-pipeline` commands can set `executionMode` and `pipelineType` on a CodePipeline pipeline.
The `aws.codepipeline.Pipeline` resource in the Pulumi AWS provider accepts `executionMode` and `pipelineType` inputs.
The link /registry/packages/aws/api-docs/codepipeline/pipeline/ targets the aws.codepipeline.Pipeline resource docs.
When two runs reach the same Pulumi stack at once, Pulumi Cloud grants the update lease to only one of them, and the other's `pulumi up` fails with an update conflict.
Azure Pipelines supports an exclusive lock check on an environment that can prevent concurrent deployments targeting that environment.
The link target /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/ exists in the Pulumi docs.
In Azure DevOps, an exclusive lock check is added from the environment's "Approvals and checks" tab.
The Azure Pipelines stage-level `lockBehavior` setting controls how a stage references an exclusive lock check.
The default value of Azure Pipelines `lockBehavior` is `runLatest`.
With `lockBehavior: runLatest`, only the most recently queued run acquires the lock, and older runs waiting behind it are passed over (cancelled/skipped) rather than eventually applied.
With `lockBehavior: sequential`, every queued stage run acquires the exclusive lock in order, one at a time.
Pulumi Cloud serializes updates to a stack one at a time in order, in the same way as `sequential` lock behavior.
The `azuredevops.CheckExclusiveLock` resource exists in the Azure DevOps provider in the Pulumi Registry and manages the exclusive lock check as code.
The `Pulumi@1` Azure Pipelines task accepts inputs `command`, `stack`, and `args`.

When two runs of the same TeamCity build configuration reach the same Pulumi stack at once, Pulumi Cloud grants the update lease to only one, and the other's `pulumi up` fails with an update conflict.
TeamCity's default is to let build configurations run concurrently against as many free agents as are available.
TeamCity's build configuration advanced option "Limit the number of simultaneously running builds" defaults to 0 (unlimited).
The TeamCity option "Limit the number of simultaneously running builds" is found under the build configuration's General Settings.
With TeamCity's "Limit the number of simultaneously running builds" set to 1, a second build is queued behind the first and runs only after it finishes.
Pulumi Cloud's per-stack lease gives one-at-a-time behavior for updates to a stack.
A link target exists: /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/ page describing update conflicts.
In Azure Pipelines, adding an exclusive lock check to the environment targeted by the deployment job serializes Pulumi deployments.
In Azure Pipelines YAML, the stage-level setting `lockBehavior: sequential` makes runs queue sequentially against an exclusive-lock-checked resource.
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/azure-devops/ has a section anchored 'serialize-deployments-with-an-exclusive-lock'.
AWS CodePipeline pipelines support an execution mode setting with a value `QUEUED`, which runs waiting executions in turn.
The default AWS CodePipeline execution mode (SUPERSEDED) lets a newer execution supersede an older execution that is still waiting to start.
